markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If Adam Hamilton's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Kansas, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Kansas at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was Hamilton 50.1%, Marshall 46.0% (Hamilton +4.1), so Adam Hamilton's polling margin is +4.1 points. Adam Hamilton outperforms if the certified margin of victory is greater than +4.1 points.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the percentage change in the seasonally adjusted Market Composite Index in the first MBA Weekly Applications Survey release after market Issuance is above -10%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying is the first-published percentage change in MBA’s seasonally adjusted Market Composite Index in the first new Weekly Applications Survey results release after market Issuance. All strikes use the same release, including strikes added later.

The reported change is used directly, including holiday adjustments and regardless of the comparison period; no calculation is required. If separate changes are reported for multiple reference weeks, the latest reference week controls. Increases are positive, decreases negative, and unchanged is 0%. “Above” means strictly greater than the strike.

Later revisions, corrections, and subsequent releases are ignored. If publication is delayed, trading remains closed pending the qualifying release, subject to the latest expiration and the contract’s missing-data provisions.
